about: A western lowland gorilla: a knuckle-walking great ape.
rules: Knuckle-walker: the arms are much longer than the legs, so the body slopes down from the shoulders to the rump; the hands rest on the middle phalanges of folded fingers, the feet flat (plantigrade) with an opposable big toe.

The hands and feet are hands: a palm, a thumb, four fingers with nails, bare dark skin on the palms and soles. Build the fingers of the knuckle-walking hand as a folded block with the knuckle row on the ground.
Huge shoulders and arms, a barrel chest, a big belly, short legs; the neck is buried in the shoulders and the head carried low and forward.
Hair is short over most of the body and longer on the arms; the chest, face, palms and soles are bare skin.
